entries.title: The world server no longer crashes with many units close together
entries.body: A line-of-sight check could write past the end of its work list and end the server process without a crash report (Windows error 0xC0000409). It now stops safely at the limit.

entries.title: Experimental Linux server build
entries.body: A Linux build of the server, compiled in Docker on Ubuntu 26.04, is published as an unsigned package for testing. The Manager cannot install it yet.

entries.title: SquidBots builds follow the latest stable module release
entries.body: Nightly builds select the latest stable release tag and pin its exact commit. Bundled release identifiers and settings metadata are supplied to the Manager.

entries.title: Interrupted SquidBots database imports require recovery before restarting
entries.body: Base imports record a pending marker before SQL starts and clear it only after SQL and history recording succeed. A later start detects unfinished imports and requests recovery instead of accepting partially filled tables as complete.

entries.title: SquidBots preserves imported bot databases and skips SQL when disabled
entries.body: Imported installer and update histories prevent SQL replay. Each base file preserves complete existing tables, creates entirely missing tables, and stops on partial structure. Existing bot data without history requires repair. Disabled SquidBots skips SQL.

entries.title: Disabled SquidBots no longer require their database to start the server
entries.body: The server skips registering SquidBots when their master switch is off. Enabling or disabling the module takes effect after a world-server restart; upstream module sources remain unchanged.

entries.title: Large SQUID database imports no longer use the short query timeout
entries.body: Initial imports larger than one megabyte receive up to fifteen minutes to finish. Normal database queries keep their existing deadline, and interrupted imports remain blocked until recovered.

entries.title: First SQUID startup has time to create its initial bot pool
entries.body: The launcher waits longer for the world when SQUID is enabled. Slow initial bot creation no longer uses the three-minute readiness limit intended for ordinary restarts.

entries.title: The Auction House Bot creates its own character when enabled
Imported SquidBots servers warn before replacing their original binary
entries.body: Imports explain that the original launcher and updater check the server binary hash. Updating that binary requires an explicit choice to keep or replace it.

entries.title: Install a server from a package on Linux, running in Docker (experimental)
entries.body: Experimental. The Manager creates the database, imports the packaged baseline and starts the server in Docker containers. It needs a Linux server package and your own game data folder.

entries.title: SquidBots settings follow the options shipped by the module
entries.body: New settings use the module's descriptions, groups, defaults and value limits while retaining existing translations. Unknown formats or invalid fields use built-in controls so the settings page remains available.

entries.title: SquidBots shows its bundled release and includes it in problem reports
entries.body: The Bots and Modules pages and problem reports include the release identifiers. Imported repacks use their recorded bot revision; empty tags are hidden. The settings file's source commit is not presented as the build revision.

entries.title: The NPC Enchanter card explains how to place and remove the NPC
entries.body: The card now shows the two commands: `.npc add 601015` where you stand, and `.npc delete` on the targeted NPC.

entries.title: One button collects all diagnostics, including crashes and Windows crash records
entries.body: Report a problem collects logs, crash reports and small dumps, Windows crash records, update journals and the running server programs in one file, then shows its folder. Crashes without a server crash report are no longer missing.

entries.title: Problem reports go to the right project
entries.body: Choose what the problem is about: Manager and other modules, CoA Companions, or SQUID Playerbots. The report opens in that project's GitHub page with the versions filled in. The bot system that is switched on is preselected.

entries.title: The Auction House Bot card no longer asks for a character GUID
entries.body: Turning the module and the seller on is enough: a server build with the automatic auction character creates its own account and character. The GUID field moved to the advanced settings. The buyer option hint no longer says it spends the auction character's gold.

entries.title: Server updates accept verified published migration variants without rerunning them
entries.body: Signed updates can recognise known published checksums without changing your migration history. Interrupted or failed SQL still requires recovery before retrying.

entries.title: Server updates replace older launchers adapted by the Manager for Wildcard
entries.body: Updates recognize the Manager’s own realm and import adjustments even when older metadata still records the original launcher. New server binaries receive their matching launcher; genuine custom edits still require your decision.

entries.title: Choose and remember the local network address friends use to connect
entries.body: Select an adapter or custom IPv4 address when sharing on LAN. Your choice survives restarts and mode changes; unavailable addresses show a warning instead of silently switching adapters.

entries.title: Older server packages cannot replace a newer installation
entries.body: Update checks stop offering stale packages after an update. To undo an update, use its recovery point instead of applying an older server package.

entries.title: Checking again no longer offers an already installed launcher update
entries.body: The Manager recognizes its own launcher integration while still detecting user edits and changes in newer signed packages.

entries.title: Large SQUID database imports have more time to finish on first startup
entries.body: The Manager allows up to 45 minutes when SQUID Playerbots is enabled, covering its initial database import and bot creation. Ordinary server startup and shutdown keep their existing deadlines.

entries.title: Update history conflicts are detected before server files change
entries.body: Damaged update records block changes and remain visible. Recovery checks saved copies before restoring, and unfinished updates protect backups from deletion and cleanup.

entries.title: Pending database updates remain visible when the server version matches
entries.body: SQL files are checked before replacing server files. Update and recovery attempts refresh their saved status, including errors. Backup deletion cannot race with an update.

entries.title: Diagnostic files with database checks stay readable after secrets are removed
entries.body: Removing a line that mentioned a secret could break the JSON files in a diagnostic package. Secret values are now replaced instead, so the files stay valid.
